title: VSME Pack: answer big customers' sustainability questions for small construction and facility suppliers
source: Top 50 research (Nov 2026): reframed from ideas dropped from the Top 25 report, plus new web research
summary: Big construction companies and property owners keep sending their small suppliers long sustainability questionnaires. Since the EU now says these requests should stay within the simple VSME standard, VSME Pack helps a small supplier fill in one VSME report from bills and records, and share it with every customer.
hook: "Three customers sent three different climate questionnaires this spring. I'm a painter with 18 staff, not a sustainability department."
story:
**Sara runs an 18-person painting and surface-treatment firm near Malmö.** Her biggest customers, a national construction group and two property companies, each sent a **sustainability questionnaire**: energy use, fuel, waste, accidents, gender balance, policies. One was **90 questions** in a supplier portal. Without answers she risks falling down the supplier list.

She has the raw data, spread over electricity bills, fuel cards, waste invoices and payroll reports, but no time to turn it into a report. A consultant quoted **€3,000**. She has heard that the EU now says customers should only ask small firms for the simple VSME report, but she does not know how to make one.
whyNow: The European Commission recommended the VSME standard for SMEs in July 2025 and asked large companies to limit supplier requests to it. The Omnibus I package lets suppliers under 1,000 employees refuse requests beyond the VSME level, and a delegated act turning VSME into the official value-chain cap was drafted in July 2026. Small suppliers now have one standard format they can prepare once.
evidence: The Commission adopted Recommendation (EU) 2025/1710 on voluntary sustainability reporting for SMEs (VSME) on 30 July 2025 and asked companies to limit value-chain requests to VSME information [Linklaters / Regulation Tomorrow]
Under the Omnibus I deal, suppliers with fewer than 1,000 employees can refuse sustainability-data requests beyond the VSME standard [A&O Shearman]
A draft delegated act dated 3 July 2026 (C(2026) 5011) sets out the voluntary standard that will act as the value-chain cap [draft act published by Diritto Bancario]
Platforms such as osapiens, Coolset and others already offer VSME modules, mostly as part of larger ESG suites (prices not checked) [osapiens]

whyReal.title: Requests are real and repeated
whyReal.text: Large construction groups and property owners must report on their value chain, so they ask every subcontractor and supplier. Each asks in a different format.

whyReal.title: The rules now favour one simple format
whyReal.text: With VSME as the recommended and soon official cap, a small supplier can prepare one report and send it to everyone.

whyReal.title: The data already exists
whyReal.text: Energy, fuel, waste and staff figures sit in bills and payroll exports. AI can read them, which suits Victor's document skills.

whyReal.title: Fits Jonatan's world
whyReal.text: Construction and facility subcontractors are the suppliers being asked. Same buyers as SubDocs and ExtraWork.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: Construction subcontractors, facility-service and cleaning firms, transport firms and small manufacturers with 10–250 staff that supply large EU companies.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The owner, CFO or quality/environment coordinator.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: Sweden and the Nordics, then any EU supplier asked for sustainability data (report in English plus local languages).

solution.title: Short interview
solution.text: the firm answers basic questions (sites, vehicles, staff, policies) in 15 minutes.

solution.title: Upload bills
solution.text: electricity, heating, fuel-card and waste invoices and a payroll summary are uploaded or forwarded by email.

solution.title: AI fills the VSME Basic module
solution.text: energy use, estimated emissions, waste, workforce and safety numbers are calculated from the documents, each linked to its source.

solution.title: Review and sign
solution.text: the owner checks the numbers and fills the gaps the AI marks.

solution.title: Share once
solution.text: export the VSME report as PDF/Excel and a share link for customers; map it into common customer questionnaires.

solution.title: Yearly update
solution.text: next year only new bills are needed, and the report shows progress.

must: Company interview for the VSME Basic module

risks.risk: Big customers keep sending their own questionnaires
risks.answer: Map VSME answers into the most common questionnaires; the share link plus the legal cap gives the supplier a reason to say no to extra questions.
VSME is now the reference; keep the product simple so changes are small.
Sell on avoided consultant fees and keeping big customers; offer yearly plans.

risks.risk: ESG suites add cheap VSME tiers
risks.answer: Win on bill extraction, local language and the subcontractor channel.

questions: Have customers asked you for sustainability or climate data in the last 12 months? How many?
Who answered, and how many hours did it take?
Did any customer say it affects whether you stay on their supplier list?
Where do your energy, fuel and waste numbers live today?
Would €39 a month (or €390 a year) for one report you can send everyone be worth it?
